provenance.l: Falcon Heavy — Wikipedia (22,819 kN at liftoff; side boosters and centre core as Falcon 9 Block 5 first stages; 5.2 m fairing)
Falcon 9 Full Thrust — Wikipedia (first stage 433.1 t / 22.2 t, 7,607 kN SL, 282/311 s; second stage 111.5 t / 4 t; fairing 1,700 kg)
NASA — Europa Clipper launch (Falcon Heavy, LC-39A, 14 Oct 2024; all three cores expended; 6,065 kg); second burn after a ~45 min coast

NASA — Key milestones for Europa Clipper's launch (Falcon Heavy, all cores expended): Max Q 1:07, side boosters BECO 3:03 and separation 3:07, core MECO 4:02, stage separation 4:06, fairing 4:31, SECO-1 7:53. The side boosters burn out at the published 183 s; every core runs at 100 % to T+20 s, then the side boosters at the level that ends at 183 s and the centre core at 46 % until side-booster separation. The 20 s and the 46 % are fitted to Max Q and MECO (SpaceX publishes no throttle schedule); SECO-1 (model 476.7 s against 473 s) is the independent check; the core separates 4 s after MECO
